articles.description: A template vacation policy for US organizations establishing employee time-off entitlements, request procedures, and special circumstance rules
categoryPath: Nonprofit Employee Handbook Guide: Essential Policies & Implementation
articles.contentText:
## About This Policy

The Vacation Policy provides a framework for organizations to establish clear guidelines on employee vacation entitlements, procedures for requesting time off, and rules for special circumstances such as illness or family leave. This customizable template includes all essential components of a standard vacation policy while allowing organizations to tailor specific details like vacation days, carryover limits, and notice periods to their unique needs.

## Who Needs This Policy

Any organization that doesn't have an unlimted PTO policy (https://resourceportal.antientropy.org/docs/template-privacy-notice-2). It is best practice to state vacation entitlement and vacation arrangements for termination, absence, and or sick leave within your handbook.

## The Policy

Vacation Policy - US (GoogleDocs) (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QuplcOQI7d-Pq4CpG8kXWBU_QhW5pIRTeEDCjMP5fE4/edit#heading=h.3w1ylcq7gebp)

**Legal Review: (https://resourceportal.antientropy.org/docs/legal-review) 05/2025**

articles.title: Vacation/Holiday Policy - Unlimited PTO Policy(Generic/Simple)
articles.description: A template unlimited PTO policy for organizations allowing flexible time off while documenting abuse prevention and visa compliance requirements
categoryPath: Nonprofit Employee Handbook Guide: Essential Policies & Implementation
articles.contentText:
## About This Policy

This is a simple unlimited vacation or holiday policy. It basically says you can take as many days as you want as long as you are doing a good job and gettting your work done.

## Who Needs This Policy

Even though an organization has an unlimited leave policy, it is still important to have documented what would be considered abusing the policy.

Sponsored Worker or Visa Employees

Note that if you have Visa or Sponsored Workers, even with an unlimited leave policy, for visa requirements you may still need an absence policy. And you will ***very likely*** need to track/log Sponsored Worker days off.

## The Policy

Unlimited PTO Policy (Generic/Simple (https://docs.google.com/document/d/18oRAUYcjYqqR64OmZImS0rQfKr3z37HG6hUyC4GAv9U/edit?usp=sharing))

articles.title: Washington D.C. Nonprofit, Charity, and Legal Entity Setup
articles.description: A guide for incorporating a nonprofit in Washington D.C. and obtaining tax-exempt status and charitable solicitation licenses
keywords: D.C. Department of Consumer and Regulatory Affairs
articles.contentText:
### Who is this article for?

Anyone wanting to start a nonprofit or charity in the state of Washington.

Nonprofits operating in Washington, D.C., are governed under the D.C. Nonprofit Corporation Act of 5. Here are the steps to starting a nonprofit or charity in this state.

### Washington D.C. Nonprofit and Charity Overview

- Incorporate with the D.C. Department of Consumer and Regulatory Affairs (DCRA)
- Apply for tax-exempt status with the IRS (https://resourceportal.antientropy.org/docs/applying-for-charity-status-us)
- Apply for tax exemptions with the D.C. Office of Tax and Revenue
- Apply for a Basic Business license for charitable solicitations with the DCRA

### Items Needed During This Process

- Registered Agent (https://resourceportal.antientropy.org/docs/us-registered-agent)
- Articles of Incorporation (https://resourceportal.antientropy.org/docs/articles-of-incorporation)
- Board Members (https://resourceportal.antientropy.org/docs/nonprofit-board-member)
- Bylaws (https://resourceportal.antientropy.org/docs/us-corporate-bylaws)

### D.C. Department of Consumer and Regulatory Affairs (DCRA)

All nonprofit organizations must first incorporate in D.C. with the DCRA (https://dcra.dc.gov/). According to the law, you only need one incorporator to proceed, but a minimum of 3 individuals to serve as directors.

**Required Documents for Filing:**

- Form DNP-1 (https://dcra.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/dcra/publication/attachments/Art_Incorp_Dom_NonProfit_Corp_DNP_1.pdf)
- Articles of incorporation. These should have the following information:
 - Name of the corporation
 - You can search whether your nonprofit name has already been taken here (https://corponline.dcra.dc.gov/Home.aspx/Landing).
 - Whether the corporation will have members
 - Name of the initial registered agent and agent's address in D.C.
 - You can find a list of commercial registered agents in D.C. here (http://www.district-of-columbia-registered-agents.com/).
- Statement that the corporation has been formed under the D.C. Nonprofit Corporation Act, Title 29, Chapter 4
- Name and street address of each incorporator
- Each incorporator must sign and date the articles
- You can also include the following information in your articles of incorporation:
 - Names of initial members of the board of directors (Minimum of 3 board members)
 - Names of initial members, if any
 - Provisions required for the corporation to meet the requirements of 501(c)(3)
 - Provision for the indemnification of directors
 - Any provision related to:
 - Purposes of why the corporation was formed
 - Management of affairs of the corporation
 - Powers of the corporation and board of directors
 - Rights and limitations of members

**Steps for incorporating:**

- File two original copies of the required documents, signed by incorporators
- Pay the filing fee of:
 - $80 - 15 days processing time
 - $100 - Same-day expedited service
- Mail all forms and required payment to:
 Department of Consumer and Regulatory Affairs
 Corporations Division
 PO Box 92300
 Washington, DC 20090
 Phone: (202) 442-4400

Bylaws are not filed with DCRA, but it’s best to have them drafted. You can find a sample of bylaws here (https://resourceportal.antientropy.org/docs/us-corporate-bylaws).

### D.C. Office of Tax and Revenue

Under certain circumstances, organizations can request exemption from local income and franchise taxes, sales and use taxes, and personal property taxes from the state. It’s best to file promptly after receiving the IRS determination of exemption, as the D.C. exemption will be retroactive to the IRS’ effective date.

**Required Documents for Filing:**

- Form FR-164 (https://dmv.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/otr/publication/attachments/fr-164_rev12-07applicationpackage_0.pdf)
- Form FR-500 (https://mytax.dc.gov/_/#1) (filed online)
- Determination or ruling letter from IRS
- Certificate of Incorporation from the D.C. Department of Consumer and Regulatory Affairs, Corporations Division
- If not incorporated in DC, provide a photocopy of the Certificate of Authority
- Copy of a lease, District of Columbia Occupancy Permit

Mail/fax the requirements to:
 Government of the District of Columbia
 Office of Tax and Revenue
 P.O. Box 556
 Washington, D.C. 220044-0556
 Fax # (202) 442-6882

### Charitable Solicitations (Fundraising) Registration

D.C. requires nonprofits to file for a Basic Business License (https://business.dc.gov/quick/9750) with the DCRA for charitable solicitations. Here are the steps:

- Request for a Clean Hands Certificate (https://otr.cfo.dc.gov/page/certificate-clean-hands) online
- Request for the following from the Office of the Zoning Administrator:
 - Certificate of Occupancy (https://dob.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/dob/publication/attachments/DOB-Certificate-of-Occupancy-Application-Requirements-and-Application.pdf), if you’re operating out of an office location. File and email to doapp@dc.gov.
 - Home Occupation Permit (https://aca20.dcra.dc.gov/CitizenAccess/Login.aspx?ReturnUrl=%2fCitizenAccess%2fCap%2fCapApplyDisclaimer.aspx%3fCapType%3dBuilding%2fHome%2520Occupation%2fNA%2fNA%26Module%3dBuilding), if you’re conducting business out of a home.
- Apply for a Basic Business License (https://mybusiness.dc.gov/login) online.
 Requirements:
 - Certificate of Occupancy or Home Occupation Permit
 - Charitable Services Business Worksheet (https://dcra.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/dcra/service_content/attachments/Charitable%20Services%20Business%20Worksheet%20%28Fillable%29.pdf)
 - Corporate Registration
 - IRS Determination Letter
 - Tax Registration
- Pay the corresponding fees:
 - Charitable Exempt - No Fee
 - Charitable Solicitation - $412.50

articles.title: Who is an Independent Contractor? (UK)
articles.description: A reference guide defining independent contractor status in the UK and explaining the key factors that determine self-employment classification.
articles.contentText:
An independent contractor in the UK is a self-employed worker or sole trader (https://resourceportal.antientropy.org/docs/sole-trader) that runs their own business and is responsible for its success and failures. They are not paid through the PAYE (Pay As You Earn) (https://resourceportal.antientropy.org/docs/pay-as-you-earn-paye) system and do not have the same rights and responsibilities as an employee.

In the UK, you can be both employed and self-employed at the same time. (i.e. You work for an employer during the day and run your own business after office hours).

**The UK would consider you self-employed if:**

*Significant Factors:*

- You can decide how, where, and when you do your work.
- You have several clients at the same time.
- You provide the main items of equipment to do your work.
- You submit invoices to clients after work has been completed.
- You operate under a contract for services or consultancy agreement that uses the terms ‘self-employed’, ‘consultant,’ or an ‘independent contractor.’

*Other factors:*

- You sell goods or services to make a profit.
- You put in bids or give quotes to get work.
- You charge an agreed fixed price for your work.
- You are in charge of paying your taxes and National Insurance.

Once you have established your employment needs, ensure you have determined what structure is best for your business for tax purposes, hiring needs, and future growth. There are several business structures with varying benefits, see the most common ones: sole trader (https://resourceportal.antientropy.org/docs/sole-trader) and PLC (https://resourceportal.antientropy.org/docs/private-limited-companies-plcs) to determine which is best for you and how to register.

articles.title: Who is an Independent Contractor? (US)
articles.description: A reference explaining IRS definitions of independent contractors, their tax obligations, and legal distinctions from employees for US businesses
articles.contentText:
In the U.S., Independent Contractors are often called:

- Self-employed person
- Sole proprietors
- Single-member LLCs
- 1099 employees

The IRS (https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15a#en_US_2022_publink1000169466) has clear definitions on what constitutes an independent contractor. The general rule is that a worker is an independent contractor if the payer controls the result of the work but not how the work will be done. Misclassifying a worker as an employee or independent contractor (https://resourceportal.antientropy.org/docs/independent-contractor-guidance) has liabilities to a company, which include the potential loss of eligibility for unemployment protection and malpractice insurance protection.

#### **Independent Contractor Designations:**

- Provide independent, specialized, or requested services on a project or as-needed basis
- Pay their own Social Security and Medicare taxes
- Not eligible for unemployment insurance or workers' compensation
- Not eligible for statutory employment benefits
- Generally not covered by labor and employment laws
- The employer does not withhold or report taxes on an independent contractor’s services

Once you have established your employment needs, ensure you have determined what structure is best for your business for tax purposes, hiring needs, and future growth. There are several business structures with varying benefits; see the two most common Sole Proprietorship (https://resourceportal.antientropy.org/docs/sole-proprietor-vs-single-member-llc) and Single-Member LLC (https://resourceportal.antientropy.org/docs/sole-proprietor-vs-single-member-llc-usa) to determine which is best for you and how to register.
